hypothesis: On current main, the already-async Python prewarm is correct for paint, but concurrent first-touch callers can consume and lose the in-flight startup handle, causing duplicate interpreter launches and lifecycle races.
approach: TS-parity-first source audit; replayed the base double-start on a Prime VM before edits. Replaced the consumed startup JoinHandle with a shared watch receiver in pa-core/kernel/provisioner.rs, froze predecessor stop gate at startup creation across retries, and added four integration fixtures for join/error cause, waiter abort, stop, and dispose during boot. Frozen unrelated surfaces unchanged.
parity_notes: TS interactive-mode.ts:1858 starts UI without waiting; agent-session.ts:10900-10908 prewarms asynchronously; tools/ipython.ts:462-482 shares managerPromise and :638 awaits it at first touch. Existing Rust create/background prewarm preserved; shared startup watch makes concurrent Rust callers join one in-flight boot, retains true failure message, keeps abort local to waiter, and lets stop/dispose await the same boot. No new async paint cut.
